scenes.tts: Can a retina full of spikes still fail to sharpen the brain's map?
scenes.visual: Title card: Correlation, Not Just Spikes. Two schematic spike rasters, both with plenty of spikes, one in correlated sweeps, one scattered. Label: schematic.
scenes.narration: Can a retina full of spikes still fail to sharpen the brain's map?

scenes.tts: This test reads a different map. Not which eye, but where in the eye.
scenes.visual: Label switch: from which eye, in the LGN, to where in the eye, in the superior colliculus.
scenes.narration: This test reads a different map. Not which eye, but where in the eye.

scenes.tts: Label a few neighbouring ganglion cells. In the superior colliculus, in the midbrain, their axons end in a zone, small if the map is sharp.
scenes.visual: A small labelled patch on the retina; its axons run to the superior colliculus and end in a termination zone.
scenes.narration: Label a few neighbouring ganglion cells. In the superior colliculus, in the midbrain, their axons end in a zone, small if the map is sharp.

scenes.tts: Todd McLaughlin, Christine Torborg, Marla Feller and Dennis O'Leary studied mice lacking the beta two nicotinic subunit.
scenes.caption: Todd McLaughlin, Christine Torborg, Marla Feller and Dennis O'Leary studied mice lacking the beta2 nicotinic subunit.
scenes.visual: Credit card: McLaughlin, Torborg, Feller and O'Leary, 2003. Label: beta2 knockout mice.
scenes.narration: Todd McLaughlin, Christine Torborg, Marla Feller and Dennis O'Leary studied mice lacking the beta2 nicotinic subunit.

scenes.tts: In their recordings, these mice had no waves in the first week. Yet their ganglion cells fired often, without correlation.
scenes.visual: The mutant's raster: plenty of spikes, scattered, no sweeps. Label: first postnatal week, in one study.
scenes.narration: In their recordings, these mice had no waves in the first week. Yet their ganglion cells fired often, without correlation.

scenes.tts: Predict. By day eight, are the mutants' zones small, or broad?
scenes.caption: Predict. By day 8, are the mutants' zones small, or broad?
scenes.visual: Normal and mutant collicular outlines side by side, the mutant zone hidden behind a question mark. On screen: postnatal day 8.
scenes.narration: Predict. By day 8, are the mutants' zones small, or broad?

scenes.tts: Broad. Normal mice had small zones; the mutants' stayed broad.
scenes.visual: Reveal: normal, small focal zone; beta2 knockout, broad zone.
scenes.narration: Broad. Normal mice had small zones; the mutants' stayed broad.

scenes.tts: Later waves and vision did not fix them, which points to an early window.
scenes.visual: A timeline: glutamatergic waves, then eye opening; the mutant zone stays broad. Label: an early window.
scenes.narration: Later waves and vision did not fix them, which points to an early window.

scenes.tts: In these recordings they had plenty of spikes, but not the normal correlation between neighbours.
scenes.visual: The two schematic rasters again, both with plenty of spikes; the correlated one is ticked. Label: schematic, spike counts not matched in the experiment.
scenes.narration: In these recordings they had plenty of spikes, but not the normal correlation between neighbours.

scenes.tts: Later labs found altered, not absent, waves in these mice. So the safe claim is narrower.
scenes.visual: Small note: later labs, altered rather than absent waves.
scenes.narration: Later labs found altered, not absent, waves in these mice. So the safe claim is narrower.

scenes.tts: Normally patterned activity, not just spiking, is needed early for the map to sharpen.
scenes.visual: On screen: normally patterned activity, not just spiking, is needed early.
scenes.narration: Normally patterned activity, not just spiking, is needed early for the map to sharpen.

scenes.tts: Last, a detector for together. A frog's tectum normally gets axons from one eye.
scenes.visual: A frog with its optic tectum highlighted; one eye's axons reach it.
scenes.narration: Last, a detector for together. A frog's tectum normally gets axons from one eye.

scenes.tts: Martha Constantine-Paton and Margaret Law gave frog embryos an extra eye, so two eyes shared one tectum.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Constantine-Paton and Law, 1978. A frog with a third eye; two eyes' axons enter one tectal lobe.
scenes.narration: Martha Constantine-Paton and Margaret Law gave frog embryos an extra eye, so two eyes shared one tectum.

scenes.tts: The two projections formed alternating stripes, where none normally exist.
scenes.visual: The tectum shows alternating bands of the two projections.
scenes.narration: The two projections formed alternating stripes, where none normally exist.

scenes.tts: Hollis Cline, Elizabeth Debski and Constantine-Paton then laid A P V on the tectum. It blocks N M D A receptors.
scenes.caption: Hollis Cline, Elizabeth Debski and Constantine-Paton then laid APV on the tectum. It blocks NMDA receptors.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Cline, Debski and Constantine-Paton, 1987. A slow-release polymer sheet on the tectum. Label: APV, an NMDA receptor antagonist.
scenes.narration: Hollis Cline, Elizabeth Debski and Constantine-Paton then laid APV on the tectum. It blocks NMDA receptors.

scenes.tts: These receptors pass little current unless glutamate is bound and the membrane is already depolarized. So they can report coincident input.
scenes.caption: These receptors pass little current unless glutamate is bound and the membrane is already depolarized. So they can report coincident input.
scenes.visual: An NMDA receptor: glutamate bound, magnesium in the pore; the membrane depolarizes and magnesium leaves; calcium enters. Label: a coincidence detector.
scenes.narration: These receptors pass little current unless glutamate is bound and the membrane is already depolarized. So they can report coincident input.

scenes.tts: Predict. What happens to the stripes while A P V is on the tectum?
scenes.caption: Predict. What happens to the stripes while APV is on the tectum?
scenes.visual: The striped tectum under the APV sheet, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Predict. What happens to the stripes while APV is on the tectum?

scenes.tts: The stripes were lost, while the retinal axons still responded. After A P V was removed, the stripes returned.
scenes.caption: The stripes were lost, while the retinal axons still responded. After APV was removed, the stripes returned.
scenes.visual: The bands blur and mix; the sheet is removed; the bands return. On screen: stripes return within two weeks.
scenes.narration: The stripes were lost, while the retinal axons still responded. After APV was removed, the stripes returned.

scenes.tts: In the frog, keeping the stripes needed these receptors. Which detector sorts the two eyes in the mammalian thalamus is less clear.
scenes.visual: Two labels: frog tectum, NMDA receptors needed to keep the stripes; mammalian LGN eye segregation, detector unresolved.
scenes.narration: In the frog, keeping the stripes needed these receptors. Which detector sorts the two eyes in the mammalian thalamus is less clear.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: timing is the address. In the models, inputs compete, and the evidence so far says that patterned firing, not just spike count, matters for which inputs stay.
scenes.visual: Closing card: Timing is the address. In the models, inputs compete. Patterned firing, not just spike count, matters for which inputs stay.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: timing is the address. In the models, inputs compete, and the evidence so far says that patterned firing, not just spike count, matters for which inputs stay.
